{
  "hook": "Edna Valley's intense marine winds completely rewrite the rules for California Grenache in this bottling. Instead of the typical 15% alcohol jam-bomb, the 1772 series delivers a tightly coiled, peppery red clocking in at just 13.8% ABV. This is a sun-loving grape forced to shiver, resulting in crunchy red fruit rather than baked preserves.",
  "wine_summary": "Tolosa built its reputation on Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, but their 1772 Grenache proves that Edna Valley's extreme coastal climate works wonders on Rhône varieties. The east-west orientation of the valley funnels freezing Pacific air straight from Morro Bay and the Pismo Gap, stalling sugar accumulation in the grapes. While Paso Robles Grenache just an hour north bakes into dark, figgy richness, Tolosa's iteration retains a bright, tart cherry profile laced with white pepper. The '1772' tier represents their estate-focused, barrel-selected lots, aiming for structure and tension over sheer fruit weight.",
  "terroir_expression": "Ancient volcanic ash and tuff form the bedrock beneath Positas and Diablo clay loams on the valley floor, providing rapid drainage that forces the Grenache vines to root deeply. This water stress, combined with the daily assault of marine fog and afternoon winds, thickens the grape skins. You taste that struggle directly in the wine's pronounced tannic grip—which is unusual for Grenache—and a distinct crushed-rock minerality that anchors the wild strawberry and thyme notes.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fermentation management here focuses on taming the grape's naturally oxidative tendencies while building mid-palate weight. The winemaking team employs careful punch-downs—manually breaking the cap of grape skins at the top of the fermentation tank—to extract color and spice without pulling harsh, bitter seed tannins. Aging primarily in neutral and lightly toasted French oak allows the delicate floral and white pepper aromatics to survive unmasked by vanilla or wood char.",
  "food_pairing": ["Duck confit with cherry gastrique: The tart red fruit in the wine mirrors the sauce, while the bright acidity cuts through the rich, cured duck fat.", "Nashville hot chicken: The wine's moderate 13.8% alcohol won't fan the flames of the cayenne paste, and the chilled red fruit provides a cooling contrast.", "Grilled portobello mushroom burgers with gruyère: Earthy, savory notes in the Grenache latch onto the umami of the mushrooms and the nutty melted cheese."],
  "comparable_wines": ["A Tribute to Grace Grenache, Santa Barbara County — Shares the same commitment to low-alcohol, high-aromatic, cool-climate California Grenache.", "Comando G Garnacha, Sierra de Gredos — Mirrors the pale color, bright acidity, and tight, mineral-driven structure found in high-altitude Spanish expressions.", "Qupé Grenache, Edna Valley — A regional peer that similarly benefits from the San Luis Obispo marine layer to preserve freshness."],
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry red with bright acidity and peppery red fruit",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink this within the first five to seven years of the vintage to catch the vibrant strawberry and white pepper aromatics at their peak.",
  "value_assessment": "At roughly $75 a bottle, you are paying a premium for a grape that often costs half as much when grown in hotter, higher-yielding regions. When compared to luxury Paso Robles Grenache like Linne Calodo or Booker, the price aligns with the market rate for high-end Central Coast Rhône varieties. It justifies the cost if you specifically value restraint and acidity over dense fruit extraction.",
  "market_position": "Pinot Noir collectors who want to branch out without sacrificing acidity are the target demographic for this bottling. You will find it on progressive California wine lists positioned as a lighter alternative to heavy Syrah or jammy Zinfandel, appealing directly to drinkers who prioritize food-friendly structure.",
  "insider_take": "Do not buy this expecting a massive, brooding Châteauneuf-du-Pape clone. The 13.8% ABV is the dead giveaway that this drinks more like a spicy, structured Pinot Noir than a traditional Grenache. It is a highly specific expression of the Edna Valley wind, but fans of rich, sweet-fruited reds will find it too lean.",

parsed.hook: Edna Valley's intense marine winds completely rewrite the rules for California Grenache in this bottling. Instead of the typical 15% alcohol jam-bomb, the 1772 series delivers a tightly coiled, peppery red clocking in at just 13.8% ABV. This is a sun-loving grape forced to shiver, resulting in crunchy red fruit rather than baked preserves.
parsed.wine_summary: Tolosa built its reputation on Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, but their 1772 Grenache proves that Edna Valley's extreme coastal climate works wonders on Rhône varieties. The east-west orientation of the valley funnels freezing Pacific air straight from Morro Bay and the Pismo Gap, stalling sugar accumulation in the grapes. While Paso Robles Grenache just an hour north bakes into dark, figgy richness, Tolosa's iteration retains a bright, tart cherry profile laced with white pepper. The '1772' tier represents their estate-focused, barrel-selected lots, aiming for structure and tension over sheer fruit weight.
parsed.terroir_expression: Ancient volcanic ash and tuff form the bedrock beneath Positas and Diablo clay loams on the valley floor, providing rapid drainage that forces the Grenache vines to root deeply. This water stress, combined with the daily assault of marine fog and afternoon winds, thickens the grape skins. You taste that struggle directly in the wine's pronounced tannic grip—which is unusual for Grenache—and a distinct crushed-rock minerality that anchors the wild strawberry and thyme notes.
parsed.vinification_summary: Fermentation management here focuses on taming the grape's naturally oxidative tendencies while building mid-palate weight. The winemaking team employs careful punch-downs—manually breaking the cap of grape skins at the top of the fermentation tank—to extract color and spice without pulling harsh, bitter seed tannins. Aging primarily in neutral and lightly toasted French oak allows the delicate floral and white pepper aromatics to survive unmasked by vanilla or wood char.
food_pairing: Duck confit with cherry gastrique: The tart red fruit in the wine mirrors the sauce, while the bright acidity cuts through the rich, cured duck fat.
Nashville hot chicken: The wine's moderate 13.8% alcohol won't fan the flames of the cayenne paste, and the chilled red fruit provides a cooling contrast.
Grilled portobello mushroom burgers with gruyère: Earthy, savory notes in the Grenache latch onto the umami of the mushrooms and the nutty melted cheese.
comparable_wines: A Tribute to Grace Grenache, Santa Barbara County — Shares the same commitment to low-alcohol, high-aromatic, cool-climate California Grenache.
Comando G Garnacha, Sierra de Gredos — Mirrors the pale color, bright acidity, and tight, mineral-driven structure found in high-altitude Spanish expressions.
Qupé Grenache, Edna Valley — A regional peer that similarly benefits from the San Luis Obispo marine layer to preserve freshness.

When compared to luxury Paso Robles Grenache like Linne Calodo or Booker, the price aligns with the market rate for high-end Central Coast Rhône varieties. It justifies the cost if you specifically value restraint and acidity over dense fruit extraction.
parsed.market_position: Pinot Noir collectors who want to branch out without sacrificing acidity are the target demographic for this bottling. You will find it on progressive California wine lists positioned as a lighter alternative to heavy Syrah or jammy Zinfandel, appealing directly to drinkers who prioritize food-friendly structure.
parsed.insider_take: Do not buy this expecting a massive, brooding Châteauneuf-du-Pape clone. The 13.8% ABV is the dead giveaway that this drinks more like a spicy, structured Pinot Noir than a traditional Grenache. It is a highly specific expression of the Edna Valley wind, but fans of rich, sweet-fruited reds will find it too lean.
